page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a 945 GB local disk, and the instance supports Premium Storage configurations. No GPUs are included in this server configuration.

The x86_64 architecture of the Intel Xeon processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), including AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets.

In benchmark evaluations, the D16ds_v7 exhibits strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 35.66 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.92 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng registers at 16997.2, while the Passmark CPU score is 27311.65, both falling within the average range. For small-model LLM inference using a 135M model, the instance achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 354.35 tokens per second, though prompt processing for the same model remains average at 1929.37 tokens per second. Large-block memory write bandwidth is measured at 54.82 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the inclusion of a 945 GB local disk alongside 64 GB of RAM provides a balanced hardware profile for general-purpose workloads without requiring separate storage attachments. Given the average database operations score of 8347.97 and Redis SET throughput of 27.91 million operations per second, this server is suited for relational databases, static web serving, intermediate-scale ETL tasks, and lightweight machine learning inference utilizing CPU-based AMX instructions.
